title: PRD build readiness
summary: A build-readiness decision. Marks each requirement testable or not, traces requirements to goals and non-goals, checks for gaps, and has engineering, design and QA review independently. A “cannot proceed” from any role blocks. The product owner and engineering lead accept the decision.
notes: The QA reviewer writes a test case for each requirement; a requirement with no writable test is untestable.
Link designs and research so requirements the designs contradict can be flagged.

config.instructions: List the problem, each goal, success metric, numbered requirement, non-goal, open question and dependency. Include requirements hidden in prose.

fields.name: id
fields.label: Id
fields.description: Its id or number as written (e.g. FR-3), if any

fields.name: blocking
fields.label: Blocking
fields.description: For an open question: whether it is marked blocking

fields.name: data_source
fields.label: Data source
fields.description: For a metric: where its data comes from

config.instructions: Apply these checks to items of kind requirement only; mark every other item not_applicable.

checklist.label: Observable acceptance criterion
checklist.question: Does the requirement have an observable acceptance criterion?

checklist.label: No vague terms
checklist.question: Is the requirement free of vague terms such as fast, easy or intuitive?

checklist.label: Not compound
checklist.question: Does the requirement state one thing (not several joined with and/or)?

checklist.label: Non-functional requirements carry a number
checklist.question: If it is a non-functional requirement, does it carry a number (a threshold, a limit, a percentage)?

config.question: Each requirement serves a goal and none falls under a non-goal; each goal has requirements

checklist.label: Conflicting requirements
checklist.question: Are the requirements free of conflicts with each other? Name any pair that conflicts.

checklist.label: Empty, error and edge states
checklist.question: Are empty, error and edge states specified?

checklist.label: Permissions
checklist.question: Are permissions (who can see and do what) specified?

checklist.label: Migration
checklist.question: Is migration of existing data or users addressed?

checklist.label: Metrics have baseline, target and data source
checklist.question: Does each success metric have a baseline, a target and a data source?

checklist.label: Designs agree
checklist.question: Do the linked designs agree with the requirements? Name any requirement a design contradicts. Mark not_applicable if no designs are linked.

checklist.label: Open questions have owner and date
checklist.question: Is every open question either resolved, or marked non-blocking with both an owner and a date? Answer not_met when any open question lacks one of these (it blocks the build); partly_met only when every open question is marked non-blocking with an owner but one lacks a date.

reviewers.label: Engineering
reviewers.brief: Review as the engineer who must build it: can each requirement be estimated? Flag requirements too vague to size, hidden technical dependencies and unstated constraints.

reviewers.label: Design
reviewers.brief: Review as the designer: are the states and flows defined for every requirement, including empty, error, loading and permission states? Flag flows that stop or branch without a defined screen.

reviewers.label: QA
reviewers.brief: Review as QA: write a test case for each requirement. A requirement with no writable test is untestable; list each one and why.

config.instructions: The product owner and the engineering lead each accept the build-readiness decision, or edit it; it is final only once both have. Check that each open item has an owner.
